komba.name: Komba
komba.origin: Komba was a mute Native American who was hired by the evil scientist Dr. Klutch to be his bodyguard. So fearsome was Komba that none of Klutch's other henchmen dared enter Klutch's hideout while he was there. In 1941, Komba was on side when Klutch brought the captured Tough Kid Squad to his hideout so that he could experiment on the twin brothers Wally and Tom Danger. The two brothers were injected with a serum that brought their bodies to the peak of their mental and physical abilities, and Klutch sought to extract it and use it for his own evil ends. After extracting a blood sample from Wally, Klutch and Komba were attacked by the rest of the squad who just broke free. During the fight, Wally stared down Komba, forcing him to flee with Dr. Klutch. On the way out, he knocked over a candle, causing the house to set on fire. Knowing that the boys would likely escape through his secret tunnel, Klutch injected Komba with Wally's blood, endowing him with the powers brought by the serum and sent Komba after the boys. Battling them in the tunnels, Komba was frightened to death when Tough Kid member and fellow Native American Eagle clubbed him with a cat tied to a stick.
powers: When endowed with Dr. Danger's formula, Komba was brought to the peak of his physical and metal capacities.

kometes.name: Kometes
kometes.origin: One day 4000 identically sized holes filled with an unknown reddish dust were discovered in Forest Park in St. Louis. As the police investigated the phenomenon, the story was leaked to the local press. Soon cult members from all over the state flocked to the sight proclaiming the end of days. When Daimon Hellstrom showed up to investigate the occurrence with Katherine Reynolds and her friend, he was instantly recognized as being the Son of Satan who had fought Baphomet days before. The crowd wrongly believed Hellstrom to be the cause of the phenomenon and attacked him, during the ensuing ruckus Hellstrom's soulfire accidentally hit one of the strange holes. Soon all of the holes were on fire, giving rise to the form of Kometes, who flew into the sky and then remained motionless, a beacon of unknown events. Hellstrom and his associates returned to his study to learn more about the creature from his texts on arcane lore and the supernatural. They soon found what they were looking for, it seemed that Komentes was to herald great cataclysm in the world, with the last time he appeared signaling the sinking of Atlantis. Indeed, around the world, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, and tidal waves seemed to signal the impending destruction of the earth, or at least another cataclysm this time around. As a result, Hellstrom decided to use his powers to go back in time to that period in order to ask the sorceress Zhered-Na how to stop the creature. After escaping capture in the ancient city of Atlantis, Hellstrom was connected mentally by Zhered-Na who got him to join her on the astral plane where she could show him how to stop Kometes. She brought him to the Primal Matrix, the model on which the universes are structured, where he saw Komentes. Approaching the matrix, the Son of Satan was attacked by its sentinel, Spyros. In the course of their battle, Spyros hurled his mighty axe at Hellstrom, but missed and instead struck Kometes, seemingly killing it. While the great cataclysm still took place in ancient Atlantis, Kometes disappeared in the modern period as well.

kono sanada.name: Kono Sanada
kono sanada.origin: Kono Sanada was a former Sumo wrestler who became a mercenary and hitman for hire to profit from his abilities. He was first seen along with his sister Sheoke, also known as the assassin Snapdragon, when he was one of a group of assassins hired to take down the Black Widow. The assassins were unsuccessful in their goal. Sheoke was later killed by the mercenary turned adventurer Diamondback in revenge for an attempt on her life. Diamondback and her allies Captain America, Zachary Moonhunter, and the Americop were later investigating Kono's employer Damon Dran, and Kono took advantage of the opportunity to try and avenge his sister's death by attempting to kill Diamondback. He was prevented from doing so by Moonhunter, and although the heroes were captured, they eventually overpowered their captors and escaped. Kono's current whereabouts are unknown.
abilities: Kono is a skilled hand-to-hand combatant, with particular skill in Sumo wrestling. Although not superhuman, his bulk gives him a greater degree of resilience than most normal humans.

koor.name: Koor
koor.origin: thumb|left Koor was the provider of the Fall People and was torn by deciding whether to burn their land to plant foreigners' oil palms, even though he didn't want to, but they didn't have many options left if they didn't want to run out of food. After the incident of the Roxxon "Pangean Horizon" oil rig, Ka-Zar, seeing him absent, asked Koor if he was not well and he replied that he was praying and that having no other resources he too would set fire to their forest to allow the palm oil cultivation of foreigners. In the end he decided to burn the land to give it to oil palm plantations. Not being able to bear the shame of having set fire to the lands of his fathers, after telling his wife that he had thus ensured food for her and their daughter, he was overwhelmed by the flames and committed suicide in the fire.

kor konn.name: Kor-Konn
kor konn.origin: Kor-Konn was a member of Attuma's barbarian horde. He captured Namor the Sub-Mariner and brought him before Attuma, not realizing that Namor had been playing possum in order to get close to Attuma. Namor then defeated Attuma in combat. Attuma later joined forces with Dorcas and Tiger Shark to destroy Namor, and Kor-Konn was a part of Attuma's forces. The villains captured the Hydro-Men except for Dr. Jennings. When Jennings notified Namor of the situation, Kor-Konn led a force against Namor but was defeated. Namor and his ally Doctor Doom led a final charge against the villains. Kor-Konn and his men fought against Doctor Doom. However, Doom killed Kor-Konn and his men by striking two missiles together.

kora lemuria.name: Kora (Lemuria)
kora lemuria.origin: Kora was a girl who was offered as sacrifice to the Zemadar (a giant reptilian creature) in the pits of Tsargol. She was saved by Thongor of Valkarth and Karm Karvus, the former then killing the sark Drugunda Thal. The archdruid Yelim Pelorvis immediately claimed the position of sark and unleashed waves of soldiers to slay the two warriors. Thongor and Karm Karvus were able to repel their aggressors and protect Kora until Sharajsha the Wizard came to their rescue using magic to disassemble them and the Nemedis to extract them. Kora awarded Thongor with a kiss. As the group was heading to Patanga for their quest, they intended to land Kora to her village, and Kora wished to pray Trianda, the Luck goddess, for their success. She also assisted to the halving of the Star Stone.

kordazt.name: Kordazt
kordazt.origin: The Monitors were Ingesteev, Kordazt, and Nygorn, three members of the Marvanite race. Hailing from the planet Marvan, they came from a society that had reach the pinnacle of perfection. With no further drive to improve themselves, the Monitors were formed and sent out into the cosmos to find inhabited worlds and determine if they were worthy of continued existence. To assist them on this mission they also included three humanoid robots named Kallara, Milandra and Askare who helped operate their testing devices. Over the centuries the Monitors found no world that fit their rigid ideas of perfection and they were destroyed. However with each planet they eliminated, their three robots grew to have emotions and became horrified by what they were charged to do. Ultimately they reached the planet Earth and here Kallara and her fellow robots enlisted the aid of the novice hero Nova and the Fantastic Four's Thing to try and stop the Monitors. During the ensuing battle, Ingesteev and Kordazt were slain fighting the heroes. With their mission aborted, Nygorn was offered an ultimatum from his former slaves: return with them to Marvan to convince their ruler, King Suzerain the errors of his way. Not wishing to do battle with his foes, Nygorn conceded and left with the three female robots.

korea katie.name: Korea Katie
korea katie.origin: The woman known as Korea Katie was a South Korean woman who betrayed her people to join the of China during the Korean War. She joined a guerilla army unit that operated from a small town where she posed as a bar tender. There, she drugged American soldiers and took them prisoner to try and learn information to stage raids on American supply trucks. She almost succeeding in capturing American soldiers Combat Kelly and Cookie Novak had it not been for the intervention of a Korean freedom fighter who helped free them. Korea Katie was then captured and turned over to the American military as a prisoner of war. Somehow, Korea Katie managed to escape and recaptured Combat Kelly and Cookie Novak in order to torture them and learn information about American troop movements. While Cookie was subject to a water torture, Combat Kelly was strapped to a spinning wheel while Katie threw knives at him. However, Combat managed to break free, and assisted Korea Katie's sister Koo in escaping execution. As it turned out, Koo was hunting her sister to avenge the shame she brought upon her family for joining with North Korea. The pair rescued Cookie from his torture in a cave, and they all fled. When Korea Katie and her troops tries to chase after them, Koo tossed a stick of dynamite into the cave entrance, blowing it up and seemingly killing Katie and her soldiers. Somehow, Korea Katie survived and still desiring revenge against Combat Kelly and Cookie Novak for their constant interference she tracked them down and prevented them from being eliminated by the Yalu River Rosie so she could kill them herself. However her chance for revenge was foiled by the interventions of the Panther Lady, Yalu River Rosie, Muktong Mollie and General Olga other enemies of the two Americans who also sought the right to get revenge. Ultimately the five women began to fight among themselves allowing Combat and Cookie to free themselves and take them all prisoner.
weapons: Katie used throwing knives and a pistol.

korless.name: Korless
korless.origin: In the late 37th-early 39th century, Korless was a member of the Clan Chosen. Roughly in the late 36th century, Apocalypse ascended to power and ruled much of North America unchallenged, for 100 years, where humans and whoever else resistant to his rule could be killed at any moment. The Clan Askani were the only rebellion left to opposed Apocalypse's rule. Years later, following the destruction of Apocalypse, by the Askani'son, and the destruction of the Askani Sisterhood, by the New Canaanites led by Ch'vayre and Stryfe, Korless joined the Clan Chosen, an Askani-inspired team of freedom fighters. Training in the Askani ways under surviving Askani elders, the Clan Chosen repeatedly battled the New Canaanites and the Scions of Apocalypse, led by Stryfe. The Clan Chosen also clashed with the Neo-Canaanites, a group that also wished to claim Apocalypse's power. Korless' demise came when he aided Stryfe in infiltrating the Clan's camp and Stryfe psychically attacked Nathan, captured Tetherblood, and the Professor. 2000 years in the past, Aliya found Cable and brought him to their time. After revealing his deceit, Korless thought that he could capture Cable and his companion, but they body-slid away and he was left with nothing to give Stryfe. For his incompetence, Stryfe killed Korless.

korrek.name: Korrek
korrek.species: Warrior Prince of the extra-dimensional realm of Katharta
korrek.origin: ===Early Life=== Korrek the Barbarian is a knight warrior and a prince of the extra-dimensional world of Katharta. Korrek the Barbarian normally wields a sword that projects mystical fire. ===The Man-Thing and Howard the Duck=== Korrek and his allies crossed over from their home reality due to a disturbance in various dimensions which was caused by serious events taking place in the Man-Thing's Citrusville swamp and made worse by interference via the demon-lord Thog the Nether-Spawn. Korrek emerged in the Earth-616 reality through a jar of peanut butter that was partially eaten by Andy Kale and spread with a knife which later became the warrior's sword. Korrek met Jennifer Kale, Andy's older sister, and the Man-Thing once he was fully in the Earth-616 dimension. Korrek worked with the Man-Thing and Howard the Duck, who was also brought to Earth due to the cracks in reality. The strange trio of friends was then attacked by a warrior force sent by the Congress of Realities until the wizard Dakimh the Enchanter banished the Congress. Dakimh transported the team to his Castle in the Sky over the Land Between Night and Day, along with Jennifer. The team travelled to Therea to stop Thog and the Congress from overtaking that reality. The Man-Thing was later actually able to temporarily destroy Thog. ===Klonus and Mortak the Usurper=== Korrek returned home to his reality of Katharta. On his return, he discovered that his father, the king, had been murdered, and that an evil sorcerer named Klonus had taken over his kingdom. Klonus took Korrek as a slave for one whole year, until Jennifer and the Man-Thing were sent to rescue him by Dakimh. The three of them helped Korrek overthrow Klonus and his barbarian ally, Mortak the Usurper, although Dakimh was killed by Klonus during the fight. ===Bzzk'joh=== Korrek teamed up with Dakimh, Jennifer, Howard and the Man-Thing again to batlle the demon Bzzk'joh. Korrek kept working with Jennifer, the Man-Thing, and Howard on future missions protecting the different realities.
abilities: Swordsman: Korrek the Barbarian normally wields a sword that projects mystical fire.

Korrek worked with the Man-Thing and Howard the Duck, who was also brought to Earth due to the cracks in reality. The strange trio of friends was then attacked by a warrior force sent by the Congress of Realities until the wizard Dakimh the Enchanter banished the Congress. Dakimh transported the team to his Castle in the Sky over the Land Between Night and Day, along with Jennifer. The team travelled to Therea to stop Thog and the Congress from overtaking that reality. The Man-Thing was later actually able to temporarily destroy Thog. ===Klonus and Mortak the Usurper=== Korrek returned home to his reality of Katharta. On his return, he discovered that his father, the king, had been murdered, and that an evil sorcerer named Klonus had taken over his kingdom. Klonus took Korrek as a slave for one whole year, until Jennifer and the Man-Thing were sent to rescue him by Dakimh. The three of them helped Korrek overthrow Klonus and his barbarian ally, Mortak the Usurper, although Dakimh was killed by Klonus during the fight. ===Bzzk'joh=== Korrek teamed up with Dakimh, Jennifer, Howard and the Man-Thing again to batlle the demon Bzzk'joh. Korrek kept working with Jennifer, the Man-Thing, and Howard on future missions protecting the different realities.

korumbu.origin: Korumbu was a Romani medicine man who lived deep in the woods, concocting potions and remedies of various sorts for his people. One day he was approached by Hugo Barge, who demanded a reducing potion to help him lose weight. Korumbu was, in fact, working on just such a potion, but it had not yet been perfected, and Korumbu feared that it was too dangerous to be used yet. Barge, however, insisted and threatened to tell the authorities where the band of Romani were hiding. Korumbu therefore gave Barge the potion he sought. After Barge took the potion, he proceeded to lose weight at a rapid rate. Barge tried to seek out Korumbu to help him, because he had to constantly eat in order to keep from wasting away. Korumbu, however, has not been seen since.

kosrouschah.name: Kosrouschah
kosrouschah.origin: The mercenary Lunatik, accompanied by Skreet, boarded Kosrouschah's private battle-star Perish IV. When he barged into Kosrouschah's chambers, the general assumed he was a prostitute and boasted that he had swallowed bigger men whole. In response, Lunatik knocked Kosrouschah's head off and confiscated an STB which the general had seemingly been using to pirate cable. Space bounty hunters Monark and Paradox made off with a spacecraft given as a wedding present to Paradox by Kosrouschah (described as "a sadist" and "a kinky little piece of cybernetics"), Paradox having assumed the form of a woman resembling Kosrouschah's mother. Enraged at the deception, Kosrouschah caught up with the bounty hunters, and attacked them and Wolverine with a P'Tah, a Pheragot and a Scatter. He was defeated when Paradox shot him through the helmet with his wrist laser.

kotik.name: Kotik
kotik.origin: Kotik was a tiger cub whose streak lived in the Siberian tundra. When Sabretooth was being carried away by Omega Red, he slit his arm, hoping a predator would follow the trail of blood and serve as a distraction and allow him to break free from Omega Red. The plan worked and the tigers attacked Omega Red, giving Sabretooth a chance to escape. However, Omega Red was overpowered by the animals and asked for help, prompting Sabretooth to pity him and return to help. After Creed killed the adult tigers, Omega Red noticed the cub and decided to keep it as a pet. The cub was initially aggressive but warmed up to them quickly. Omega Red later decided to name it Kotik. While he predominantly appeared to be Omega Red's pet, Creed took care of him at times when Omega Red was busy fighting.

He was shown to be very loyal, going so far as to growl at and chase after Vassily, who had been tormenting Omega Red for months. kourtney keaton.name: Kourtney Keaton
kourtney keaton.origin: Kourtney Keaton was an actress who briefly dated the Human Torch, a member of the Fantastic Four. A vain woman who only sought fame, Kourtney merely dated the Torch to boost her celebrity profile, something that the Torch was fine with, as it also helped with his own celebrity. However, her relationship with Johnny became strained when the Fantastic Four lost their fortune. After the team was evicted from the Baxter Building, Johnny attempted to move in with his new girlfriend. By this point, Kourtney had decided to break up with Johnny and pursue a relationship with a famous Hollywood actor. When this didn't work out, Kourtney returned to New York, where she renewed her relationship with the Torch, who had just obtained a job with the New York City Fire Department. Eventually, Kourtney and Johnny drifted apart, with Kourtney moving to Los Angeles to film a movie, though Johnny sounded out his suspicions about how Kourtney was also doing it to be in the vicinity of the famous Hollywood actor she was chasing.

Together with his brother Dyngo, Koyoti accompanied Prince Hyinar to Centauri-IV in order to find super-powered individuals from whom they could steal their abilities. After Prince Hyinar and Dyngo used stolen abilities to abduct members of a crew of Inhumans that had recently landed on Centauri-IV, as well as the members of the Universal Inhumans that were accompanying them, Koyoti gained the empathic abilities of Swain and the All-Knowing. When Hyinar targeted the remaining members of the Inhuman crew as well as the Universal Inhuman Court, who were investigating a Skyspear in the Great Desert, Koyoti used his abilities to take control of Maximus the Mad, who was in turn possessing the Univeral Inhuman Court. When the group of depowered Inhumans previously captured by the Snarks escaped captivity, Gorgon managed to toss Marvel Boy's weapon to Medusa. Medusa used the gun to blast Koyoti's head off.

kozar.origin: General Kozar was known for his ambitions to overthrow King Hapwell and establish a tyrannical regime, but he was deeply plagued by cowardice and fear, preventing him from openly acting against the king. Determined to overcome his innate fear, Kozar sought out a gypsy sorcerer and demanded a spell that would allow him to face battle without fear and without taking damage. The sorcerer, recognizing Kozar’s evil nature, created a potion that granted the desired effect—but with an unusual consequence: Kozar was transformed into a toy soldier. In this form, he became completely impervious to danger during battles, gaining absolute courage without the fear of being harmed.

As such, during the 16th Century Kraggoom took a spaceship and traveled to Earth, landing in Britain. Before he had a chance to put his scheme into action, others of his kind landed on Earth and captured him. Though the peaceful cloud people were unable to harm one of their own, it was decided by their elders that since Kraggoom was a repeat offender, he would be made to spend the rest of his life adrift in Outer Space. He was then sent out an airlock and remained floating around the vicinity of Earth for centuries, waiting for his chance for vengeance. His chance came when astronaut Derek Wolfington became the first man to attempt a trip to the moon. Wolfington, however, was ill-fitted to the task, having forged all of the necessary records and psychological evaluations to make himself appear to be the prime candidate for the job. Upon blasting off into space, the mental strain was too much for Wolfington who began to crack under the pressure. Kraggoom invaded the spacecraft and attacked Wolfington, planning on continuing with his original plan of fusing their minds and using the man's body to take over the world. Unfortunately this added shock was the last straw for Wolfington's fragile mind and he entered a semi-catatonic state and would possess life-long amnesia about the events that happaned in space. It seems that whatever happens to his human host's mind, also happens to Kraggoom's, as he also found himself blacking out with a state of amnesia. As a result, Wolfington inadvertently saved mankind from the menace of Kraggoom. It is reasonable to assume that Kraggoom may still exist in Wolfington's sub-consciousness, but whether or not he ever emerges from his state of amnesia remains to be seen.

kraig.name: Kraig
kraig.origin: Kraig was ridiculed by people throughout his life for his grotesque appearance and childlike mentality which caused him to want to strike out at anyone whom he believed was laughing at him. In an undisclosed incident Kraig also lost his right hand which was replaced with a powerful metal one by his benefactor Agatha Timly and her husband Nathan. Kraig acted as the couple's servent under the belief that they woul ultimately help him regain his real hand. Nathan brought the Werewolf by Night, Jack Russell, back to his home as his wife believed him to know the whereabouts of the powerful dark magic tome the Darkhold. Jack had no idea what the couple were refering to and was thus chained in the basement until he co-operated. During one night of interigation, Kraig was hurting Russell too much for Nathan's liking and Kraig lashed out at the man, accidently killing him. Jack took the opportunity to escape in the confusion, but was later turned into the Werewolf at the dawning of the full moon. He then went back and confronted Kraig again, though the powerful man-servent almost defeated the Werewolf. As he was preparing to deal the final crushing blow, his mettalic hand was struck by lightning, instantly killing him.
weaknesses: Kraig seemed to possess the mental faculties of a child.

krakken.name: Krakken
krakken.origin: Krakken was geokinetic mutant, and an engineer. During the war against humans, Krakken ran the Krakken Works, designing and manufacturing machines to get rid of the "human monsters", working with Holocaust. His plant was once attacked by the human terrorist known as the Red Prophet, who tried to destroy it and murder the workers, but Krakken defeated him using his seismic gifts. Krakken lost and eye to Prophet, but mentioned to have killed him (though it could have been a lie to reassure his son). He married Sasha and had a son, Isaac, to which he would tell tales of the war and reassuring him about the Prophet and the humans no longer being a threat. As the leader of the X-Terminated, Prophet, retaliated killing him in his own home, where his wife (seemingly neutralized by Prophet) and children slept.
powers: Krakken stated that his seismic gifts could tear the Earth in two, though that might have been an exaggeration.
abilities: Red Prophet stated that his skills as an engineer were far greater than his mutant gift.

krakoa moira vii 1.name: Krakoa (Moira-VII.1)
krakoa moira vii 1.origin: With Mister Sinister corrupting the Quiet Council of Krakoa, the island nation slowly began to conquer Earth. Using an orbital cannon designed by Forge, the Sinisters lobotomized Krakoa, not before killing killed Cypher, allowing them to free the original Mr. Sinister and gain full control of the island. Prompted by rumors of renewed Eternal aggression, the dual nations of Krakoa and Arakko launched an attack on the Eternals. As per the peace treaty of Judgement Day, the Arakkii unleashed Uranos and defeated the Eternals. Five years later, the Arakkii began to grow suspicious of their Krakoan cousins. Storm confronted the Quiet Council and learned of their corruption at the hands of Sinister. The Arakkii prepared for war, but were counseled by Destiny to wait. The Arakkii grew their strength, but it was ultimately futile. The Krakoan Sinisters launched a massive invasion of Arakko, bolstered by Chimeras. Using a Legion-clone, they were able to destroy Mars and Arakko with it.

krakos.name: Krakos
krakos.origin: Krakos was an Atlantean sleeper and a member of Cell-13. He along with the rest of the cell had been altered to appear human and breathe and operate on the surface world. Kratos and the rest of the cell were led by Kamar, the estranged son of Namor. They were assigned by Zoran to go to the surface and use their new powers to attack various U.S. targets. The first target for the cell was at random as they ended up in the small town of Bentonville, Kansas. They found a young man there called Jacob Anderson, who they tortured to death and carved gills into his neck. Kamar and Krakos then left Arath to his task as he detonated himself and killed about 1000 people. The team then traveled to the city of Seattle, with the plan to construct a device to absorb all the moisture from the air, causing all the humans in the city to suffocate. During the mission the trio killed an innocent bystander called Marv just for getting too close. Arath grew impatient with the plan, but Kamar was able to persuade him to hold back for the right moment. The Atlantean terrorists disguised as garbage men set up the final component to the extractor device. Krakos then killed another human by tossing him the back of the garbage truck. They surveyed the city and their future victims from the top of the Space Needle. The team still kept their disguises as they traveled to Unocorp building and trapped a number of humans inside, which included John. All the humans were doomed to be killed by the extractor device. Namor the Sub-Mariner then arrived to stop the terrorists and destroy the device, but Krakos punched down to the ground before he could destroy the device. Kamar then revealed himself to his estranged father and how everything he was to blame. Namor was taken back by his son's presence, and just stood there as his son explained his deep hatred for him and the humans he protected. Namor then realized his opportunity to destroy the machine but was grabbed by Arath who absorbed his powers. Arath pulled him into the air and beat him repeatedly, until Namor was able to rip off his duplicated ankle wings, causing the Arath to fall to his death and be impaled on the Space Needle. Krakos was later knocked out by Namor. His fate is unreveald, but it can be presumed that he was taken back to Atlantis by Namor along with the other surviving members of Cell-13.
abilities: Skilled in hand to hand combat

krattaka.name: Krattaka
krattaka.origin: Krattaka was the sole survivor of her planet, which was devoured by Galactus. She joined another group of survivors of Galactus in Newhaven, a hidden planet inhabited exclusively by the last members of their respective species. When the Silver Surfer and his companion Dawn Greenwood arrived by accident to Newhaven, they attracted the attention of Galactus, who followed the Surfer's trail of cosmic energy to Newhaven. Even after Dawn tried to sacrifice herself to become the Devourer's new herald to spare Newhaven from destruction, its inhabitants decided it was better to leave the planet for Galactus to devour, and they fled. Because he was the reason Galactus destroyed Newhaven, the Silver Surfer promised the former inhabitants to find them a new planet, and he became their herald. Surfer's deed came to an end once he discovered a planet with a adaptive atmosphere that allowed all of the survivors from different species to live on it. After months of inhabiting this "New Newhaven," the Silver Surfer discovered it was actually a living planet called Euphoria, that used its adaptive atmosphere to defend itself from the survivor's grief by inducing them happiness and controlling their actions to ensure their well-being. A group of the survivors decided to leave the planet as they didn't want to be Euphoria's puppets, including Krattaka, but the vast majority remained on it.

When the Silver Surfer and his companion Dawn Greenwood arrived by accident to Newhaven, they attracted the attention of Galactus, who followed the Surfer's trail of cosmic energy to Newhaven. Even after Dawn tried to sacrifice herself to become the Devourer's new herald to spare Newhaven from destruction, its inhabitants decided it was better to leave the planet for Galactus to devour, and they fled. Because he was the reason Galactus destroyed Newhaven, the Silver Surfer promised the former inhabitants to find them a new planet, and he became their herald. Surfer's deed came to an end once he discovered a planet with a adaptive atmosphere that allowed all of the survivors from different species to live on it. After months of inhabiting this "New Newhaven," the Silver Surfer discovered it was actually a living planet called Euphoria, that used its adaptive atmosphere to defend itself from the survivor's grief by inducing them happiness and controlling their actions to ensure their well-being. A group of the survivors decided to leave the planet as they didn't want to be Euphoria's puppets, including Krattaka, but the vast majority remained on it.

krauss and polly.name: Krauss and Polly
krauss and polly.origin: Krauss was a spy for the Nazis during World War II. A blind man, the cause of his lack of vision is unknown, he claims to have lost his vision in combat -- but this may have been a lie. Krauss loved birds and kept many, and trained them how to speak and carry out his orders and used them in his subversive activities. In the early 1940s, he worked on the "Boebachter" newspaper and was part of a German-American Bund before it was shut down. Settling in a home in New York City, he regularly visited an institute for the blind. He also began posing as a fortune teller with a unique twist: His parrot Polly would be the one giving the fortunes. He sought government officials and coated Polly's beak with a poison that was instantly lethal. When the parrot read the victims' palm, the bird scratched them, and they soon died of the poison. These strange deaths soon attracted the attention of the FBI who were unable to determine the cause of death. The head of the New York branch then sought the aid of the Angel to help solve the case. By this point, Krauss had targeted the FBI head and had Polly read the man's fortune. Krauss got away before the poison could affect the FBI agent, but it gave the Angel the clue needed to track Krauss down. Contacting the city's many institutes for the blind, the Angel got in touch with Dr. White, a man who dealt with Krauss in the past. They then planted a false story on the radio about how White had a vital clue proving Krauss to be the killer. As expected, Krauss came to White's apartment and sent Polly up to poison White. Instead of White, the bird fought with the Angel, who bound the bird in the hopes of luring Krauss up to the apartment. Krauss took the bait; however, the Angel underestimated the blind man who was able to knock him out and escape White before the doctor could shoot him. Krauss rescued Polly and escaped in a taxi cab. However, the Angel followed him back to his neighborhood and was able to determine which house belonged to Krauss by finding one of Polly's feathers outside. Going in, the Angel was captured when he fell through a trap door. Krauss then had the Angel bound in his basement where he intended to unleash his birds, all of whom had been starved so that they would consume the Angel's flesh. The Angel broke free and smashed through the observation booth's window and ran off to collect the authorities, leaving Krauss to deal with his bird. When the police arrived on the scene, they found that the birds had eaten Krauss alive.
abilities: Although blind, Krauss had an acute sense of hearing, able to single out a specific voice in a crowd. He was also a skilled fighter and an expert bird trainer.
weapons: Krauss often used birds as his weapons, particularly his parrot named Polly

kray tor.name: Kray-Tor
kray tor.origin: Kray-Tor was a Judge and Inquisitor for the Universal Church of Truth. He was killed by Adam Warlock with the Soul Gem while he was holding a trial against Warlock for crimes against the Church. In this trial he accepted lying witnesses and false evidence provided by the Church's prosecutor. Warlock on the other hand had to put up with a mute defender who was nothing more than an eye and fell asleep. After being swallowed by the Soul Gem, he lived on Soulworld alongside Autolycus and other Black Knights of the Universal Church and later even with Warlock and his friends Gamora and Pip the Troll. When Thanos was resurrected by Mistress Death prior to the Infinity Gauntlet affair, he briefly met the Silver Surfer who was sent to Soulworld by the Titan. Later, when Warlock battled the soulless Count Abyss, he briefly lost the Soul Gem to Abyss who wanted to use the Gem to restore his soul which he had sold to Zalkor. When he tried to utilize the Gem, he disrupted Soulworld and the Oneness of Being in it, which had a disturbing effect on Kray-Tor. Though he hoped that Adam would restore this Oneness after he got the Gem back, instead Warlock used Kray-Tor's Soul to attack Abyss. Kray-Tor isolated himself from the other Residents of Soulworld and planned to leave Soulworld, maybe in order to take Revenge against Adam Warlock.

kris keating.origin: Keating was a New York City Police Department SWAT leader. He headed a special powers task force against superhumans. He was eventually killed and impersonated by agents of the Foreigner who assigned the impersonation as a rotating test. He blamed the heroic Defenders for all the damages caused by their recent battles, and informed them that they were not going to get away with it. He was aware of the team's address in Long Island and threatened to send them a bill for the damages.

kriss lout.name: Kriss Lout
kriss lout.origin: Kriss "Gabby" Lout was a Nazi spy who was active during World War II. In the fall of 1943, he had secured a position as a janitor at the Defense Department office. His cover as a spy was soon exposed when he placed poisoned tipped needles in the ear pieces of all the phones in the building, killing the soldiers answering them. When the Human Torch and Toro began investigating Lout's whereabouts, they paid a visit to the boarding house he was staying. In order to throw the heroes off his trail, Lout disguised himself as his landlady Mrs. Fagan and allowed the two heroes to search his room. Although they found evidence proving that Lout was the killer, they were unable to determine where he went. However, the Torch soon deduced that Lout was posing as Fagan, and they chased the spy into a secret chamber inside the house. There, the two heroes briefly had their flames doused when they flew into a pit of water, but climbed out and captured "Gabby" and his henchman before they could set off a bomb to destroy the White House. Lout's subsequent fate is unknown.

krista.name: Krista
krista.origin: thumb|left|Krista as a Valkyrie Like her sister, Hildegarde, Krista was a skilled warrior and a member of the The Valkyries. She was kidnapped by Pluto in an attempt to set the Asgardians against the Olympians. She was freed by Thor and Hercules, but was so badly injured during the fight that Thor had to change into the form of Donald Blake to save her. When Hela had taken over Valhalla and turned it into a reflection of her own realm, Niffleheim, Odin sent Krista and the rest of the Valkyrior ahead of him to fight off Hela, but she and her sisters were slain by Hela's minions. When Odin got there, he plead with her to bring them back to life and stop her madness, but she explained that after a recent encounter with Thor and Lady Sif, she realized that she had wanted to express her own feelings of compassion and desire to be a woman, but could not since she was burdened with being the goddess of death. Odin then took pity on Hela and granted her the wisdom and knowledge she sought. She went back to Niffleheilm, allowing Valhalla to return to its original form, resurrecting Krista and the rest of the Valkyries in the process. While wondering in a grass plain of Asgard, Danielle Moonstar came across a winged horse trapped in a bog. She decided to help the horse and was soon confronted by a group of riders who were after it. She was holding her own in a battle with them, but one thrown axe threatened to end her life. At that point, Mist appeared. The young Valkyrie caught the axe and scared the riders away. The two women introduced themselves to each other, and Mist discovered that her new acquaintance was from Midgard. Mist was surprised to see that the horse, Brightwind, had bonded with Moonstar, a mortal. She invited Moonstar to join herself and her sisters, failing to clarify said sisters were the Valkyries. Moonstar soon rode with the Valkyries, and Mist and the others made their visitor feel like a part of their family. Moonstar was still unaware of their actual identities. She was puzzled when she noticed other Asgardians running away from their group. Mist told Moonstar to let them be, but refused to clarify what scared the Asgardians. Later, Mist had an argument with another Valkyrie. The unnamed Valkyrie felt that the mortal (Moonstar) had no place among them and should not ride one of the sacred horses. Mist pointed that the horses choose their own champions, and this one chose Moonstar. She argued that no matter her origin, Moonstar was now one of them. Mist also urged her fellow Valkyries to explain the situation to the new recruit. Moonstar overheard the conversation and mistook a comment about sealing the bond in blood as a threat. She took Brightwind and flew away. Hela revealed to Moonstar the nature of her new powers. When the novice Valkyrie attempted to use said powers against Hela, the goddess easily defeated her. But their brief confrontation was sensed by Mist and the Valkyries, who rode to the rescue. Hela chose to retreat, not daring to strain her powers to defeat them. She was wary of an upcoming confrontation with Thor. Loki prepared to send the combined forces of the X-Men and the New Mutants from Asgard to Midgard. But first, he stated that he would strip them of all the powers, gifts, and enchantments which they gained during their stay. All except Karma, who had gained in beauty during her stay. At this point, Mist stepped forward to remind him of a second exception. She stated that by the law of Odin himself, a Valkyrie cannot be parted from her steed. They compromised by allowing Moonstar to take Brightwind with her to Midgard. Mist informed her new sister that there will a place at the Valkyries' table waiting for her. Following the departure of the mortals, Loki informed Mist that his end of their bargain has been fulfilled. She represented the Valkyries in stating that they would keep their silence concerning the events of the visit. The rest of Asgard would be led to believe that it was all a misunderstanding. In Asgard, Mist and Moonstar had a training session. They used battle staffs, and Mist quickly gained the upper hand. She pinned Moonstar to the ground. With no way to victory, Moonstar conceded defeat. Mist attributed her victory to Moonstar's lack of concentration. She queried what was in her "little sister"'s mind, and Moonstar answered that she felt as if being watched. At this point an intruder made his presence known by encasing Moonstar in a bubble. Claiming that it was time for her to return home. Mist jumped to defend her sister and battle begun. The intruder twice knocked her down, only for Mist to rise more determined than before. Meanwhile, Moonstar freed herself. Moonstar manifested chains in order to restrain Mist, who felt betrayed. Moonstar explained that she recognized the intruder to be Hotamitanio, a Cheyenne god. She reached her own understanding with the god, who departed. She then returned to Mist to explain the situation, the fight had been over

krista marwan.name: Krista Marwan
krista marwan.origin: When a repentant Death Metal realized his own evil, he sought to create a being that could destroy him someday. Taking genetic material from Madison Jeffries and Vesper, Death Metal injected his creation into the reproductive tract of the mutant empath, Krista Marwan. Vesper's team, Genetix, arrived to stop Death Metal but were soundly defeated by him, twice. Ultimately, it was Krista who quelled the misguided cyborg's rampage. Contacting him via her thoughts, she informed Death Metal that she would keep the baby, and raise him not to kill Death Metal, but to redeem him.
powers: Krista is a low-level mutant empath. She can read the thoughts and of those within her surroundings.

kristal van helden.name: Kristal van Helden
kristal van helden.origin: Kristal Van Helden was the daughter of a South African diamond miner who lost a huge amount of their fortune when the nation stopped its apartheid politics. Wanting to rebuild her fortune, Kristal kidnapped Emma Frost, planning to use Frost's diamond form to create diamonds and sell them for jewelry and body armor. To harvest the diamond, the diamond that made up Frost's body had to been grafted to living tissue. After an entire garden was turned into living diamond, Frost's telepathic power, which was being suppressed by van Helden's crystal palace, was amplified by the diamond, allowing her to take out van Halden's men. The energy overload caused van Helden's crystal castle to crumble. Emma switched to her diamond form and fled her prison unharmed while van Helden was impaled by a huge chunk of diamond and died.

kristie nord.first_appearance: Wolverine and the X-Men (animated series) Season 1 11
kristie nord.origin: Kristie Nord is the daughter of Maverick. She had memories of Wolverine seemingly killing her father when she was six years old. She harbored resentment and grudge for him for years. When Logan reappeared years later, she attacked him wanting to know why he took Maverick from her. When he said he didn't remember, she was angry but was soon knocked out by Sabretooth. She soon learned the truth, indirectly from Sabretooth, that her father had seemingly been killed by Sabretooth and that she was saved by Wolverine. Following this discovery, she attacked Sabretooth and forgave Logan. Later, she was kidnapped by Weapon X, like her father was. Mystique and Wolverine teamed up together and saved both her and Maverick. Emma Frost then restored her father's memories of her, reuniting them.
powers: She was able to change the ground into mud and cause a mudslide. She was also able to use individual rocks as projectiles and change their shape and form to trap her opponents.
abilities: She appears to be a very good horse rider.

krokwel.name: Krokwel
krokwel.origin: ===Origin and early years=== Krokwel was an Ogre mage, and served Otherworld as part of the Captain Britain Corps. Because Krokwel ingested magic, James Braddock, due to the "misperceptions" he had about those "forbidden magics", ejected him from the Corps. He and Merlyn had him relegated in the Forest of Sorrows, a place with an unquenchable appetite for sorrow, to which he was tied, sentenced for eternity to dwell there. He became the master of the ancient Lords of the Thousand Sorrows (though those ancient knights allegedly recognized only the sorrow of the forest as their masters). He resided in his pyramid. ===Modern Age=== Sentenced to be erased from reality by the Captain Britain Corps, Fantomex was rescued by Psylocke, who brought him to the Forest of Sorrows, and asked Krokwel to heal him. Krokwel first intended to let Fantomex disappear and feed Psylocke's sorrow to the children in the woods, but then offered her a deal in exchange for her sorrow and her capacity to ever feel any of it again. Once the deal was struck, Krokwel provided Psylocke and Fantomex with a "mummified dragon" to bring them to the Northern Earth Portal. He also gave Psylocke a vial of poison, in case she fell into the hands of the Goat's forces. Captured by the Skinless Man, Psylocke used Krokwel's poison to defeat him. Later, Krokwel was a speaker in Shaylee's Interdimensional Geography course at Strange Academy, on the topic of their home of Otherworld. Krokwel's presentation was cut short by Shaylee who feared that his horrific descriptions would scare her friends from visiting her.

kronaster sintariis.name: Kronaster Sintariis
kronaster sintariis.origin: Kronaster Sintariis was the Ruul ambassador to the Intergalactic Council. He manipulated the Council into punishing the planet Earth in the incident known as Maximum Security. It was later revealed that so called "Ruul" were a fabrication of the surviving Kree. The once powerful Kree Empire posed as the species known as the "Ruul" in order to manipulate the council into a gambit to get their revenge against Earth. Kronaster Sintariis brought Earth to the attention of the Council because of continued interference of Earth super-heroes in various extraterrestrial cultures; Sintariis stated that Earth should be "quarantined." To this end, the Intergalactic Council designated Earth as a penal colony and decided to send the the worst galactic criminals there.

kronnitt.name: Kronnitt
kronnitt.origin: Kronnitt was one of the gods worshipped by Desak Sterixian and his fellows. On the Cusp of Tseris, the holiest of all days to that religion, Desak's daughter Loatia was selected to be sacrificed to Kronnitt by the priests (after many fathers refused that their own daughters would be selected). Pious Desak accepted her daughter's fate, but was troubled by the ghostly apparition of the Designate who tried to persuade him from refusing to give Loatia as offering, making him seem mad in the eyes of his peers who couldn't see the apparition. The offering was without results, and caused Desak's wife Almonnas' defiance towards the gods and her husband as well. Soon, Kronnitt himself descended on the planet, displeased, accusing his flock of being blasphemers and unbelievers. The Designate came again, offering Desak the power to destroy the gods. As the Destroyer of Gods, he defeated Kronnitt and the other gods, destroying their realm and "freeing" the believers, to their own despair.
powers: From his armor, Kronnitt could projects blasts. It is unknown if he had powers (including those blasts) from his god status.

kropotkin the great.name: Kropotkin the Great
kropotkin the great.origin: Kropotkin the Great was a pompous magician that rented an apartment from April Sommers, but after he failed to pay rent or return for a long time, she gave his room along with all his furnishings to Bruce Banner. Kropotkin was indignant when he eventually returned to find his apartment occupied, but when he found out it was the Hulk, he hoped to find a way to incorporate the monster into his act. He began travelling with Jim Wilson for chances to join the Hulk's entourage.

krowtanem.name: Krowtanem
krowtanem.origin: The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse are members of the Axi-Tun race, a race of beings from the planet Tun. They are Linbythoum, Yentron, Krowtanem, and Rowregyynac, known as War, Pestilence, Famine, and Death respectively. They scoured the universe and became a scourge to all they encountered, earning them their biblical names. They sought to conquer the planet Earth at is was considered the nexus in a circle of other civilized worlds in the universe. When they attempted to conquer the Earth centuries ago, they initially found it easy pickings as it was populated by savage primitives. However, they were soon opposed by a race even more mightier than their own that defended the people of Earth and drive the Four Horsemen from the planet. They fled back to Tun, where their defeat was seen as weakness and they were exiled from their home world. Seeking to regain favor from their people, the Four Horsemen returned to conquer Earth in the modern age when they were convinced that the beings that defeated them in the past had left the Earth. Upon their arrival, Pestilence unleashed a plague that caused the entire population of Manhattan to go into a deep sleep for 48 hours. When the citizens awoke their city was under siege by rodents, disease, and strange creatures. While the city panicked the Fantastic Four came to the aid of New Yorkers and clashed with Pestilence directly. When the Thing resisted the debilitating disease that Pestilence was unleashing upon him, he caused the alien to vanish with a single blow. The FF's leader Mister Fantastic then deduced that the beings that defeated the Four Horsemen in the past had set up devices to banish them from Earth provided they were opposed. Reed then split up the team to tackle the other members of the Four Horsemen. The Human Torch and Medusa went to Africa where they found that War was escalating a combat zone by providing weapons to both sides of the conflict. Johnny and Medusa stopped the warring sides and clashed with War, defeating him in combat. But before he vanished, War removed his mask showing all gathered the real face of war: themselves. In Cambodia, Mister Fantastic and the Thing clashed with Famine, who was making the people of the country starve even though there was an abundance of food. After forcing the people to eat bowls of rice, Reed smothered Famine with his own body, until their foe vanished as well. The group reunited and traveled to Mount Everest where they found Death. He created death constructs of each member of the Fantastic Four. Realizing that fighting their own death images would be lethal, the FF switched opponents, destroying these horrifying death parodies of themselves. Medusa then threw the Thing into Death's body, striking another victory for the heroes as Death was banished from the Earth as well. The Four Horsemen were later captured by the Stranger and imprisoned on his laboratory world. When the Stranger's world was under attack by the being known as the Over-Mind, this foe freed the Four Horsemen and other captives. The Four Horsemen were later defeated by the protector of the universe known as Quasar. If the Four Horsemen were re-incarcerated or if they managed to escape remains uncertain. The group has not been seen in many years.
powers: As Famine, Krowtanem had the ability to cause others to starve, he could mentally condition them into being incapable of recognizing food as a form of torture while starving his victims.

kru.name: Kru
kru.origin: Kru the Vulture lived in the Belgian Congo during the 1930s. Young David Rand, later known as Ka-Zar, followed Kru to find Zar the lion trapped in quicksand. Later, when Ka-Zar clashed with the ape known as Bardak over possession of a mirror once owned by Paul de Kraft, Kru watched eagerly waiting for the battle's conclusion so that he could feast on the loser. Ka-Zar slew Bardak, and Kru presumably feasted on his corpse.

krumson.name: Krumson
krumson.species: Spyrican mutated via exposure to cosmic rays
krumson.origin: Krumson was a member of the inner circle of the Overseer, the patriarch of the planet Spyre. When Earth scientist Reed Richards set out to travel to Spyre aboard a rocketship, the Overseer became aware of the planned incursion and manipulated a cosmic ray storm Richards' ship had to pass through to increase its intensity and scuttle his ship. Richards and the tripulants of the ship were bestowed superpowers by the cosmic rays and turned into the Fantastic Four. Fearing that the now-empowered explorers would seek to complete their original mission, the Overseer devised a procedure to harness cosmic rays and grant his own people super-powers in hopes to stand up against the potential invaders, and Krumson encouraged the idea. Krumson was the second Spyrican to be irradiated after Eylen, who gained the ability to manipulate water. However, unlike Eylen, Krumson's transformation mutated his appearance into a disfigured monster. Because of this, Krumson was shunned and separated from his family. He was banished to the ancient ruins of the Capital City of Spyre, Lowtown. In the process, the Overseer rechristened him Scrum. thumb|left|Before his transformation Scrum was soon joined by countless other rejects, who were similarly disfigured by the cosmic rays. As Big King Scrum, Krumson led organized these outcasts into the Monster Mob. Despite his banishment, Scrum remained loyal to the Overseer. Together, they secretly staged a rivalry between the Monster Mob and the Unparalleled, a group of the few gamma mutates that aesthetically pleasing. Since Spyre was a perfect society without war or crime but the Overseer needed the Unparalleled to train to fight the Fantastic Four, Scrum regularly sent monsters into Capital City for the Unparalleled to have threats to fight. When the Fantastic Four traveled to Spyre and confronted the Unparalleled on arrival, The Thing was flung during battle into Lowtown, where he was attacked by the Monster Mob while Scrum watched. After The Thing fought through hordes of monsters, Scrum confronted him personally, but was defeated as well. The Thing refused to kill Scrum or take his subjects for himself, and instead rallied the Monster Mob into crawling their way back to Hightown to reclaim their place in society. Their rebellion was opposed by the Unparalleled, but the confrontation came to a pause when Minster Fantastic exposed to the public the fact that the Overseer had manipulated the cosmic ray storm he and his teammates attempted to pass through during their first attempt at reaching Spyre, meaning the Overseer was responsible for granting the Fantastic Four their powers. After this revelation, Scrum helped The Thing reach the top of the Tower of Over-Site to confront the Overseer. While Scrum wanted The Thing to reason with the Overseer that the Monster Mob had a place in society, The Thing lashed out at the Overseer. He was only stopped from killing him due to the intervention of the Invisible Woman, but their fight caused the collapse of the building. After the Fantastic Four made peace with the Overseer and the Unparalleled, Mister Fantastic shared with the Spyricans a temporary cure that would allow each mutate to regain their normal form once a year. Before subjecting himself to the cure, Scrum reunited with his estranged daughter, who had grown up to become the member of the Unparalleled named Kor.
powers: Mutated Form: In his mutated form, Scrum appears to possess and durability.

kruun.name: Kruun
kruun.origin: Powerlord Kruun was the overall tyrant of Breakworld, who ordered to intercept and destroy the S.W.O.R.D. spaceship where Colossus was located. When the soldiers landed, he ordered to capture and interrogate them, while he would talk to Danger. She said she could kill the X-Men and that they had that common goal, so he finally agreed because the weapon aimed at Earth needed to be protected. When he learned that Danger betrayed them and Colossus was seen with Aghanne, he spied the X-Men, who were heading in a spaceship towards the moon-based weapon. Thinking they had a secret plan called 'Leviathan', he ordered to blast the shuttle upon which Cyclops escaped; after the mutant died, he brought him back to life to interrogate him about Leviathan. He was then defeated by Cyclops' optic rays and held prisoner in his own fortress, until he was freed by Ord. thumb|left He was eventually maimed by Wolverine and dethroned by Colossus, then moved to San Francisco and bound his life force to his mate, Haleena.

krylxxa.name: Krylxxa
krylxxa.origin: Krylxxa was one of the young Phytons to venture in the outside world. To survive, she killed a young serving girl, and the townsfolk would had burned her, if Conan and Fafnir hadn't rescued her from the stake. Asking them to escort her to their people, she soon fell in love with Fafnir, and the feeling was mutual. As they arrived in the caverns and the two humans were captured and sentenced to death, Krylxxa freed them and escaped with them, knowing she could not survive in the outside world without draining the life from others, but preferring death to living apart from Fafnir. After three days, Krylxxa's life energy was spent, and though Fafnir offered to give up his own life force for her, she chose not to ever take another life. Though Krylxxa then died, Fafnir took some comfort in seeing her in any of the wildflowers and meadows they passed.

ksa alien.name: Ksa (Alien)
ksa alien.origin: Ksa was a leader of an unnamed, highly advanced, and humanitarian alien race. They discovered a form of cosmic dust traveling through the universe infecting alien races with a deadly plague. Having developed an antidote, thye provided it to the various worlds effected by the cosmic dust. By 1954 the plague had hit the planet Earth, already in the grip of the Cold War. The appearance of the plague and sightings of Ksa's flying saucer caused widespread panic and led people to believe that the alien visitors were responsible for the plague. Believing contrary, the Human Torch and Toro boarded the alien vessel and learned of Ksa's mission and agreed to try and tell the people of Earth the true intention of Ksa's visit to Earth. However, while trying to quell a mob the Torch and Toro had their flames doused and put in a room that sprayed them with water. Undaunted by his goal, Ksa landed on Earth alone and tried to present the cure to the people who surrounded his ship. The angry mob beat Ksa within an inch of his life. But Ksa managed to give the antidote as he died, making the frenzied mob realize how wrong they really were.
powers: Apparently none

kshathra vairya.origin: Allegedly, according to the ancient Zoroastrian lore, Ahura Mazda, the creator god, emerged from the personification of infinite time, Zurvan. A wise and benevolent representing truth, order and justice, Ahura Mazda started populating his domain with life. His birth was soon followed in the one of his twisted mirror image and antithesis, Ahriman, who personified deceit and chaos. Ahriman rejected the peace offerings of Ahura Mazda and tried to kill the life who had been imbued in his domain. After a prolonged battle, narrowly overcame and banished him to the Nether Realms. Kshathra Vairya, god of metal, was one of the Yazatas created by Ahura Mazda to uphold order and justice and in preparation for Ahriman's return. Banished, Ahriman created the Divs, demonic gods with the sole purpose of opposing the Yazatas. Since then, the two groups have waged an endless war against each often, often using mortals as pawn in attempt to gain the upper hand. The Yazatas ended up being worshiped on Earth in the Persian/Iranian plateau, as well as in Central Asia and India, from 1000 BC into modern days. The nexus between Earth and Elysium was indeed located on Mount Damavand in the Alborz Mountains and at Naqsh-e Rustam (within modern-day Iran).

ku var.name: Ku-Var
ku var.origin: A man legendary for cruelty and a more brutal overlord of Atlantis than Lhok-Nor, Ku-Var seemingly eclipsed him, and proclaimed himself ruler and emperor of Atlantis. His blood-thirsty tribe wiped out half the barbarian population of the island and united the other half under his absolute rule. The Sea-Mountain Tribe was betrayed by one of their own, Iraina. All males were enslaved (including the shaman Ram-Os), all females added to Ku-Var's harem, save for Iraina who became his best warrior and his favorite, though she claimed that she was no man's mistress slept alone in a locked room where even Ku-Var wasn't allowed. For the royal wedding of Princess Elise of Thule with Rashver, son of the king of Verulia, King Governi of Thule invited heads of state from all of Thuria and the surrounding islands, including Ku-Var for Atlantis, and King Kull. During the evening, Governi held a tournament. When Valusia was pitted against Atlantis, Ku-Var chose Iraina to fight Brule. The night after they returned to Atlantis, a drunken Ku-Var attempted to force himself upon Iraina, who killed him. She beheaded Ku-Var and paraded his head to his soldiers, asking them to bow down to her. They charged her and were slaughtered.

kublai khan.name: Kublai Khan
kublai khan.origin: In 1279, possibly helped by the Dragon Mr. Lao, Mongolian ruler Kublai Khan conquered China and the Song Dynasty, establishing the Yuan Dynasty, the first time China was ruled by outsiders. He controlled China for about sixty years. In 1368, Hui Lin a resident of Nanjing killed a Mongol warrior and gave him the message that the Khan's reign was over, stating that himself was the sword that would pierce Kublai Khan's heart. After a series of Khans (judged unworthy by Mr. Lao) ending with , the Yuan Dynasty was overthrown by the Ming Dynasty in 1368.

kuhomai.name: Kuhomai
kuhomai.origin: Kuhomai's father was a general in the Imperial Japanese army, who participated in the during World War II. Although this was a victory for the Japanese, General Kuhomai committed Seppuku after some unspecified failure. This, Kuhomai blamed General Douglas MacArthur who was in charge of American forces that were forced to retreat from the region during the Battle of Bataan. Kuhomai would later lead an army of Japanese soldiers in clashing with American forces located in New Guinea. Upon hearing that MacArthur was planning to visit American troops stationed there, he and his men dug an underground tunnel beneath the American base and loaded it with boxes of TNT, hoping to blow up the entire base and eliminate MacArthur in the process. However, this plot was discovered by Captain America and Bucky Barnes. The two heroes were captured and tied up in the underground cavern filled with the explosives, however they managed to break free. Cutting the ignition wires to the explosives prevented Kuhomai from detonating the explosives, and they captured the soldier sent in to see what was wrong. Cap and Bucky then pushed the explosives close to the Japanese camp then sent out the soldier to give the all-clear signal. When Kuhomai pulled down the plunger on the detonator, the resulting explosion killed him. Shortly after, an army of American soldiers led by Bucky eliminated the surviving Japanese soldiers under his command.

kuhrra daizonest.name: Kuhrra Daizonest
kuhrra daizonest.origin: Nothing is known of Kuhrra Daizonest's past, but he used his biokinetic abilities to become a renowned faith healer, making himself a fabulously-wealthy man in an otherwise poor region of Brazil. He was in truth a ruthless cult leader with a private death squad at his beck and call, and also operator of a mine where anyone who opposed him was sent. Kuhrra detected the powers of Andre Mexer, a street child in the region, and hired his squad to retrieve him for his own purposes. Mexer was also being sought by Wolverine, who hoped to recruit him for the Xavier Institute. Daizonest's thugs defeated Wolverine, killed the other street kids living with Mexer, and brought Mexer back to Daizonest. When Mexer refused to serve Daizonest, Daizonest rearranged the boy's brain chemistry, greatly decreasing his intelligence, and sent him to the mine. A vengeful Wolverine soon tracked Daizonest down, with the latter choosing to fight Logan himself. Despite Logan's fighting skill Daizonest fought him evenly, using his powers to rearrange Logan's body in the most painful ways possible, but made a grave mistake when he went in for the kill and attempted to tear Logan's heart out, finding his powers blocked by Logan's adamantium ribs. Seeing the opportunity, Logan stabbed Daizonest to death. Logan eventually rescued Mexer - or what was left of him - but was haunted by the fact that, for all intents and purposes, Daizonest had won.

weaknesses: Kuhrra's power apparently has no effect on implants or anything artificially added to a person's body like the adamantium added to Wolverine's bones.

kulkulk.name: Kulkulk
kulkulk.origin: Kulkulk was a Deviant who was born on the planet Armechadon. As an adult, he came to rule one of its provinces. One day, an enormous starship landed in his province, and Kulkulk and his guards were part of the crowd who went to look at it. As they neared it, Hept-Supht insisted that it was the Vimana, the legendary lost starship of Lord Tantalus, but Kulkulk told him to be quiet because Tantalus was just a myth. One of the new arrivals then made himself known, asking if the reason why his realm was in such disarray was because the people didn't believe in him. As those around him knelt to the being they identified as Lord Tantalus, Kulkulk remained standing. When Tantalus stated that he was less than pleased with what he saw and asked if Kulkulk ruled in his absence, Kulkulk confirmed that he ruled that province but that the Dark Lord ruled the world from the Tower of Tartarus and that he would not be unseated by the newcomer's little sham. Kulkulk then pointed out that legend said that Tantalus could kill a man with but a touch and said that if he were truly the Dreaded One but his words were cut off when Tantalus grabbed his face in one hand and used the Black Legacy to kill him. Kulkulk managed to scream "AIIIEE" as he died. After that, none of the denizens of Armechadon doubted who Lord Tantalus was, and they obeyed when he commanded them to accompany him as they went to storm the "Dark Lord" together.

kull.name: Kull
kull.species: Human; barbarian of Atlantis, later became the first notable king in the world.
kull.origin: ===Origin and early years=== Kull was born in Atlantis. An orphan, he was adopted by the tigers of Tiger Valley. He was eventually taken in by the Sea-Mountain people. Soon, he bested his fellow tribesmen in both martial and mind matters. A questioner and a seeker, he was singularly different from the rest of the tribe. When his fellow tribesmen tried and burned Sareeta for marrying a Lemurian, Kull killed her by throwing a dagger at Sareeta, sparing her from a slow death, while causing himself to be targeted by his tribe. Kull consequently fled Atlantis. ===Slave of Lemurian pirates=== Kull was enslaved by Lemurian pirates, who had him bound the oar, to serve as a galley slave and as a gladiator, where he faced a Wolf Man, with whom he forged an alliance. After two years of captivity, Kull overcome a pair of drunken guards and escaped, swimming to the shore of Valusia. ===Mercenary=== Fearing the wizard-priest Rotath of Lemuria, Asfodel IV hired Kull to slay him. Although the barbarian was successful, Rotath cursed both Asfodel and Kull before casting a spell that would allow him to eventually return to life during the Hyborian Age. ===Outlaw=== On Valusia, Kull joined a group of outlaws in the hill country, but was eventually caught and locked in the dungeons of the City of Wonders, the capital. ===Gladiator=== Due to his physique, he was sentenced to the gladiatorial arenas, where he became a sensation. Recognizing his nobility of spirit, the Valusian Count Murom Bora Ballin bought him his freedom. ===Valusian soldier=== Count Murom Bora Ballin eventually bought him a commission in the Valusian army. Eventually, Kull's natural leadership helped him rise to the rank of commander of the king's personal regiment, the Black Legion. He was soon embroiled in a plot to assassinate King Borna set by Kaanuub, baron of Blaal. Kull confronted Borna and killed him in a duel, receiving a scar on his right cheek during that fight, a symbol of the violence by which he seized the Topaz Throne and by which he would keep it. ===King of Valusia=== Upon his first public processions, Kull, aided by Brule the Spear-Slayer, Pictish ambassador to the court, uncovered the threat of the Serpent-Men and inflicted upon them the first of a series of defeats. ====Ardyon's rule / Kull in exile==== For a time, the evil sorcerer Thulsa Doom usurped the throne of Valusia, posing as Ardhyon and wearing the Serpent Crown. During that time, Kull wandered the known world, experiencing supernatural adventures. ====Return==== He eventually returned to Valusia and took back his throne. Kull decided to annihilate all those who offered human sacrifice to the dark elder gods, including Thuron, the king of a mountain city on the outer fringes of Valusia. On what was thought his deathbed, Death seduced and was seduced by Kull, and returned him to life. The deities who later became known as the Elder Gods of the Hyborian Age intended to make King Kull of Valusia the vessel of their power, but chose instead to make the immortal cat, Sedrick (felinized by Thulsa Doom) the container of their power. For this, Kull slew Thulsa Doom. Varnae, who served in the Cult of the Darkholders under Thulsa Doom, became injured during the battle. On the verge of dying, Varnae was transformed into the first vampire by sorcerers of Atlantis by using the Darkhold. The Serpent-Men were eventually (almost) exterminated with Kull's help. ====Later reign==== Kull's later reign was described as a golden age, sparked by a Kull who shared his time between expanding and defending Valusia from a side, and the "relentless pursuit of knowledge in a quest for the ultimate answers to the riddles of reality." The circumstances of his death remain unrevealed. ===Legacy=== ====Pre-Cataclysmic Age==== After Kull's rule, his name became the word used to qualify Valusia's sovereign. His line seemingly ended with Valusia when the Great Cataclysm hit the City of Wonders and caused the death of Volonius the Seventh. ====Hyborian Age==== Kull remained known during the Hyborian Age, notably in Conan's racial memories. ====Antiquity (circa 200 AD)==== The memory of Kull remained circa 200 AD through the Picts, Gonar (descendant of the eponymous Pict shaman ally of Kull), and Bran Mak Morn, king of the Picts (descendant of Brule). ====Modern Age==== Robert Howard wrote stories about King Kull circa 1932. It is unknown how Howard came to know of Kull. ==Relationship== While treating women with compassion and chivalry "beyond all reason", he stood away from the role of lover. On what was thought his deathbed, Death seduced and was seduced by Kull, and returned him to life.
abilities: King Kull was an excellent all-around armed and unarmed combatant, extensively trained in the warfare of the Thurian Age. Kull was also highly intelligent and prone to lose himself in philosophical contemplation.
weapons: Throughout his adventures, Kull preferred a battle axe as his weapon of choice. Later as King, Kull would favor a broadsword in addition to his axe. Kull wielded for a time the golden blade, and briefly held the Sword of Green Fire.
aliases: Kull the Destroyer Kull the Conqueror Kull the Magnificent Barbarian-King Warrior-King
affiliations: Valusia Formerly: Atlantis hired by Asfodel IV

Although the barbarian was successful, Rotath cursed both Asfodel and Kull before casting a spell that would allow him to eventually return to life during the Hyborian Age. ===Outlaw=== On Valusia, Kull joined a group of outlaws in the hill country, but was eventually caught and locked in the dungeons of the City of Wonders, the capital. ===Gladiator=== Due to his physique, he was sentenced to the gladiatorial arenas, where he became a sensation. Recognizing his nobility of spirit, the Valusian Count Murom Bora Ballin bought him his freedom. ===Valusian soldier=== Count Murom Bora Ballin eventually bought him a commission in the Valusian army. Eventually, Kull's natural leadership helped him rise to the rank of commander of the king's personal regiment, the Black Legion. He was soon embroiled in a plot to assassinate King Borna set by Kaanuub, baron of Blaal. Kull confronted Borna and killed him in a duel, receiving a scar on his right cheek during that fight, a symbol of the violence by which he seized the Topaz Throne and by which he would keep it. ===King of Valusia=== Upon his first public processions, Kull, aided by Brule the Spear-Slayer, Pictish ambassador to the court, uncovered the threat of the Serpent-Men and inflicted upon them the first of a series of defeats. ====Ardyon's rule / Kull in exile==== For a time, the evil sorcerer Thulsa Doom usurped the throne of Valusia, posing as Ardhyon and wearing the Serpent Crown. During that time, Kull wandered the known world, experiencing supernatural adventures. ====Return==== He eventually returned to Valusia and took back his throne. Kull decided to annihilate all those who offered human sacrifice to the dark elder gods, including Thuron, the king of a mountain city on the outer fringes of Valusia. On what was thought his deathbed, Death seduced and was seduced by Kull, and returned him to life. The deities who later became known as the Elder Gods of the Hyborian Age intended to make King Kull of Valusia the vessel of their power, but chose instead to make the immortal cat, Sedrick (felinized by Thulsa Doom) the container of their power. For this, Kull slew Thulsa Doom. Varnae, who served in the Cult of the Darkholders under Thulsa Doom, became injured during the battle. On the verge of dying, Varnae was transformed into the first vampire by sorcerers of Atlantis by using the Darkhold. The Serpent-Men were eventually (almost) exterminated with Kull's help. ====Later reign==== Kull's later reign was described as a golden age, sparked by a Kull who shared his time between expanding and defending Valusia from a side, and the "relentless pursuit of knowledge in a quest for the ultimate answers to the riddles of reality." The circumstances of his death remain unrevealed. ===Legacy=== ====Pre-Cataclysmic Age==== After Kull's rule, his name became the word used to qualify Valusia's sovereign. His line seemingly ended with Valusia when the Great Cataclysm hit the City of Wonders and caused the death of Volonius the Seventh. ====Hyborian Age==== Kull remained known during the Hyborian Age, notably in Conan's racial memories. ====Antiquity (circa 200 AD)==== The memory of Kull remained circa 200 AD through the Picts, Gonar (descendant of the eponymous Pict shaman ally of Kull), and Bran Mak Morn, king of the Picts (descendant of Brule). ====Modern Age==== Robert Howard wrote stories about King Kull circa 1932. It is unknown how Howard came to know of Kull. ==Relationship== While treating women with compassion and chivalry "beyond all reason", he stood away from the role of lover. On what was thought his deathbed, Death seduced and was seduced by Kull, and returned him to life.
abilities: King Kull was an excellent all-around armed and unarmed combatant, extensively trained in the warfare of the Thurian Age. Kull was also highly intelligent and prone to lose himself in philosophical contemplation.
weapons: Throughout his adventures, Kull preferred a battle axe as his weapon of choice. Later as King, Kull would favor a broadsword in addition to his axe. Kull wielded for a time the golden blade, and briefly held the Sword of Green Fire.
fields.notes: Kull (Kull of Atlantis, King Kull of Valusia) was created by Robert E. Howard and first appeared in " " ( , 1929). Kull was one of the characters featured in the series of Marvel Value Stamps issued in the 1970s. thumb|right|Marvel Value Stamp #21 Kull was once erroneously stated to be the leader of Red Slayers, rather than the commander of the Black Legion.

kulla.name: Kulla
kulla.origin: Kulla was the ruler of another dimension. He kidnapped scientists from Earth in order to force them to build an Electro-Death Ray to conquer the peace-loving people of his dimension. He accomplished this using a human accomplice on Earth and Henry Pym was soon targeted. Transported to Kulla's realm Pym refused to work for Kulla and found himself locked in a dungeon. Changing into Ant-Man, Pym found he could control the strange insects that lived in that realm and used them to assassinate Kulla. With Kulla defeated the rebels in his domain took over and returned Pym and all the other scientists to their home dimension.

kulra thorr.name: Kulra Thorr
kulra thorr.origin: Kulra Thorr was an adventurer from Zarfhaana and a commoner. He was the lover of Lady Delcardes, a Valusian noblewoman who lived in the Palace of the City of Wonders, but they were forbidden to marry due to Valusian custom that no noblewomen could marry a man of "peasant" birth. When he was barred the way to the palace, he slew seven guardsmen before King Kull held back the guards and stopped him. When he was explained the whole situation, Kull had Kurla Thorr exiled from Valusia. Plotting with Thulsa Doom who posed in the guise of her slave Kuthulos, Delcardes had her Old Race talking cat Saremes send Kull on a fool's errand and supposedly to his death at the hands of the people of the Enchanted Domain beneath the Forbidden Lake. Delcardes was unaware of this, wishing to have Kull believe a prophecy of the talking cat, to later have Saremes decree that she and Kulra Thorr could marry, a decree she thought Kull would have followed. It was in fact Thulsa Doom who spoke for the cat. Once the plan uncovered, Thulsa Doom fled, and Kull decided to give his blessing to Delcardes to marry Kulra Thorr. Kulra Thorr presumably married Delcardes, and his exile was presumably lifted in the process.
